messages:
ingrid_cs: Heads up — onboarding call with Zephyr. Browser SDK integration is getting repeated 429s during initial sdk.init preflight. Customer seeing this immediately after creating a session.

devon_se: Can you paste the exact error snippet they see? 429 body or headers?

ingrid_cs: From their web console: "POST /v1/preflight 429 { \"error\": \"rate_limited\" }". They also forwarded a raw response header: "x-rate-limit-reset: 24" and request id x-rw-req: rz-0a7c"

maria_platform: Which SDK + version? and are they using ephemeral token flow or static key?

ingrid_cs: Using browser-js v0.9.2 with ephemeral token refresh (server exchanges). They spin up around 12 tabs in quick QA loops.

ryan_infra: 12 tabs doing preflight can definitely hammer the handshake. Preflight is counted as a handshake request that touches token validation + quota checks. We throttle per-key and per-source IP.

alice_support: Quick mitigation we usually recommend: stagger client init, or cache one ephemeral per page for short TTL. Also bump preflight grace by adding exponential backoff on 429s.

ingrid_cs: Customer asked for a short-term unblock — they can't change QA flow today. Any server-side tweaks we can do?

devon_se: We can temporarily raise the soft rate window for that org on Hosted for onboarding (increase from 60 req/min to 240 req/min) but need approval. Also can whitelist their dev API key for 30m.

maria_platform: If we do whitelist, ensure it's scoped and audited. I'll need org id + request id and ETA. Also toggle should be time-limited.

ingrid_cs: Org: zephyr-inc (org_zeph_338). Sample request id: rz-0a7c. They tested from region eu-west-1.

ops_bot: Incident create: CS-ONBOARD-927 opened by ingrid_cs. Assigned: devon_se, ryan_infra. Priority: P2 (customer blocked on test).

ryan_infra: Before we run whitelist, ask them to send one HAR with the preflight sequence and a minimal repro (3 tabs) so we can validate it's not double-posting. Also confirm their preflight logic isn't retrying on network failures without jitter.

devon_se: For long-term: recommend client change — cache ephemeral token for at least 2 minutes per browser tab, and add jittered backoff for initial preflight. We should add a sample snippet in our quickstart: 

```js
// pseudo
async function initClient() {
  const token = await fetch('/session-token') // server mints ephemeral
  // keep token in memory, reuse for reuse window
}
```

alice_support: I'll draft a short KB for them with exact fields we need (HAR, env, X-Forwarded-For, sdk version) and a safe repro to reduce their flake.

ingrid_cs: They just sent a HAR in the thread — attaching now. HAR shows three parallel preflight posts all within 400ms.

maria_platform: That matches the rate window being tripped. Two follow-ups: 1) confirm we treat preflight + first generation as combined budget or separate? 2) check if their token endpoint is misconfigured causing repeated token refreshes.

devon_se: Answer: preflight and generation are separate counters but both count toward the per-key throughput. If they do preflight spikes followed by generation spikes, it's easy to hit the aggregate operational limits. Token refresh loops -> extra preflights.

ryan_infra: Action plan: (1) temporary soft-whitelist for org_zeph_338 for 2 hours to unblock QA; (2) CS share KB and repro and ask them to reduce parallel tabs or enable client-side token reuse; (3) engineering to add a quickstart note about preflight jitter; (4) infra to instrument the specific request-id path to see if repeated token exchanges are happening.

devon_se: I can do the whitelist now if maria_platform approves and ops_bot confirms audit entry.

maria_platform: Approved for 2 hours. ops_bot: please add audit note and expiration timestamp.

ops_bot: Audit: whitelist applied to org_zeph_338 by maria_platform until 1747784200.

alice_support: I sent the KB + repro checklist to Zephyr. They confirmed QA is unblocked and will re-run but will adopt token caching after tomorrow's deploy.

ingrid_cs: Great — I'll close CS-ONBOARD-927 once they verify. Thanks team :tada:
